Born in Lee County, Illinois, in 1880, son of Edward Clinton Wintrode and Anna Ogden,
and raised on the family farm in Hayes Township, Ida County, Iowa.
By 1905 he was at Parker, Turner County, South Dakota, on the county jury list,
and that year he married Elizabeth Fritz of Barclay, Iowa.
In 1910 they were farming in Brothersfield Township with their first two daughters.
He farmed near Parker for the rest of his life, a farmer working for himself on his 1918 draft card,
and they raised eleven children: Olive (1907) , Vivian, Charlotte, Ralph, Bernice,
Inez, Irma, Virgil and Marjorie (1920) , and the twins Maurice and Maurine, born in 1923.
By his son Maurice’s account he also speculated in land, lost much of it when farm prices collapsed in the 1920s,
and later was supervisor of the Parker public schools.
He died of a brain tumour on 14 August 1933, in Minnehaha County.
Born 30 July 1884 in Barclay Township, Black Hawk County, Iowa, daughter of John L. Fritz and Mary Ann Staebell.
She married Harry Wintrode in 1905, and they raised eleven children around Parker,
South Dakota: eight daughters and three sons.
Harry died in 1933, when she was 49 and the twins were nine; in 1940 she was head of the household at Parker,
with Vivian, Irma, Marjorie and the twins still at home.
Maurice remembered how she carried them through the dust years on county help, two cows,
chickens and what the older children could send; when the cistern ran dry they hauled water from town,
and “the precious water was used and reused in many ingenious ways.”
She died on 21 December 1951 and shares his stone at Saint Christina, Parker.
